title: Pemmican and dried meats
h1: Pemmican and dried meats: Indigenous origins, the fur trade, and what modern guidance says
dek: A food of Cree, Lakota, Dakota, Anishinaabe, Blackfoot, Chipewyan and Métis peoples, named as the sources name them. No recipe, no ratios, and an honest statement of what modern safety guidance does and does not cover.
description: Who made pemmican and wasna, how the fur trade and the Métis depended on it, and what USDA and NCHFP dried-meat guidance says. History only; no recipe.
recheck: When a Dene, Plains Cree, Blackfoot, Anishinaabe or Lakota-authored source is added, when Parks Canada or Library and Archives Canada sources are read, or if USDA or NCHFP revise their jerky guidance.

safety_review.scope: Gated (pemmican/curing). Items for the human reviewer: (1) the page gives no recipe, ratio, time or storage duration for pemmican; (2) it reproduces the 160 F / 165 F jerky heat-step figures with attribution, and states that USDA FSIS (heat before dehydrating; home jerky 1 to 2 months) and NCHFP (heat before or after drying; 2 weeks at room temperature) differ; (3) the verdict is not-validated for lack of any regulator source on pemmican. Also recommended: cultural read-through by someone with standing in the communities named, before publication.
